newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares buoyed by soft Ifo, await Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: German shares buoyed by soft Ifo, await Bundesbank.

text.p: German shares started bourse trade with solid gains on Thursday, buoyed by data indicating slower than expected economic growth in the first quarter of the year.
The DAX index was up 29.25 points at 3,382.70 points at 0926 GMT, building on a stable start in pre-bourse trade despite sharp declines on car giant Daimler-Benz.
Daimler was trading down 3.73 percent, or 5.15 marks, at 133 marks after releasing 1996 earnings late on Wednesday.
Dealers said some of Daimler's news, including plans for a convertible note issue, had proved disappointing, especially in the light of the recent rally among German car shares.
But the overall market got a boost from a report showing the Ifo institute's business climate index fell to 92.4 in March from 93.6, far below expectations for a figure of around 94.0.
Volumes were moderate ahead of the Bundesbank's annual news conference which will follow its regular policy-making council meeting later on Thursday and before Wall Street's opening.
While the Bundesbank is not expected to make a move on rates, uncertainty before its meetings regularly keeps the share market on hold.
Shares in BMW traded up 18 marks at 1,435.
BMW chief Bernd Pischetsrieder said on Wedesday that BMW was expecting "slight" earnings growth in 1997, a comment he clarified as meaning single digit percent growth.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa was little moved by a statement from the company saying its 1997 results would be above those in 1996. Its shares edged 12 pfennigs higher to 22.70.
